title: Dobby Owner Recovery Request v2
description: Wire shape of the device-key-bound owner recovery request the host exports (controlling authority: ADR-0058 § Owner recovery v2; selector namespaces: ADR-0062 § 1; observable flow: docs/specs/session-lifecycle.md). ADR-0039 is the superseded predecessor whose 5-source hardware-threshold binding this shape replaces; it is history and is not citable as current authority. Schema validity proves shape only: acceptance additionally requires the possession proof to verify against the provisioned device public key over the canonical payload bytes, purpose binding, an unexpired window, and payload/authority-context agreement. No v1 hardware-threshold request is readable.

keyId.$comment: Cross-field obligation JSON Schema cannot express: this keyId MUST equal "device-" followed by the first 16 characters of payload.recoveryPublicKeyHash, and the verifier MUST recompute it and reject a mismatch. The schema can only bound the namespace and length; accepting a device selector that is not derived from the signed public key hash would let a substituted device key present a proof under an unrelated identity (ADR-0062 device selector).

ADR-0062 § 1 canonical vendor selector <purpose-short>-<prod|test>-<YYYY-MM>. payload.vendorKeyId names the vendor recovery key the eventual response must be signed with, so only the recovery ring is expressible here; a plugin-package or license selector is a shape violation. Format conformance is not trust: the host still requires an exact match in its recovery ring.

deviceKeyId.$comment: minLength/maxLength are redundant with the pattern, which already fixes the length at 23; they are kept as defence in depth and MUST be updated together with the pattern if the derivation prefix or digest length ever changes -- a partial edit yields a $def that rejects every value. Device-side selector namespace from ADR-0062 § 1: derived, not rotated, and disjoint from the vendor selector namespace. A vendor-formatted selector in this slot, or a vendor slot carrying a device- selector, is fail-closed.

utc.$comment: Field ranges are bounded, not merely digit-counted: a two-digit-per-component pattern accepts 2026-99-99T99:99:99Z, which reaches the typed parser as an out-of-range instant and turns a shape error into a parse/arithmetic failure path (range overflow). Residual calendar validity the pattern cannot express -- 2026-02-30, non-leap 02-29 -- stays with the typed parser; leap-second :60 is deliberately outside the accepted set.
